massachusetts.medicaid_note: Massachusetts expanded Medicaid, so most adults under 65 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify for MassHealth.
massachusetts.apply_note: The Massachusetts Health Connector is where you apply online for MassHealth, and the same application can include SNAP by checking a box (SNAP itself is also applied for at DTAConnect.com).
massachusetts.agency_name: Massachusetts Executive Office of Health and Human Services (MassHealth for Medicaid; Department of Transitional Assistance for SNAP)
massachusetts.state_note: One MassHealth application can cover health coverage and SNAP at the same time — check the SNAP box on the form and it is sent to the Department of Transitional Assistance automatically.

michigan.medicaid_note: Michigan expanded Medicaid through the Healthy Michigan Plan, covering adults ages 19-64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level.
michigan.apply_note: MI Bridges is Michigan's online benefits portal, where one application covers Medicaid (Healthy Michigan Plan), SNAP food assistance, cash assistance, and child care.
michigan.agency_name: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (MDHHS)
michigan.state_note: Expedited food assistance can be approved within 7 days for households with very little money, while regular food assistance decisions take up to 30 days.

minnesota.medicaid_note: Minnesota expanded Medicaid, so adults under 65 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify for Medical Assistance, the state's name for Medicaid.
minnesota.apply_note: MNbenefits is Minnesota's online portal for SNAP, cash assistance, and emergency help, while health coverage (Medical Assistance and MinnesotaCare) is applied for through MNsure.
minnesota.state_note: Minnesota splits the application in two: use MNbenefits for food and cash help and MNsure.org for health coverage, and expect a phone interview with your county after applying for SNAP.

mississippi.medicaid_note: Mississippi has not expanded Medicaid, so coverage is mainly for children, pregnant people, parents with very low incomes, and people 65 or older or with a disability, and most childless adults do not qualify no matter how low their income is.
mississippi.apply_note: Access Mississippi is the state's online portal for applying for Medicaid, SNAP, and other benefits run by the Division of Medicaid and the Department of Human Services.
mississippi.agency_name: Mississippi Division of Medicaid and Mississippi Department of Human Services (MDHS)
mississippi.state_note: Parents qualify only at very low incomes (about 24% of the poverty level), but pregnancy coverage now lasts 12 months after the birth.

missouri.medicaid_note: Missouri expanded Medicaid in 2021, so adults ages 19-64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify for MO HealthNet, the state's name for Medicaid.
missouri.apply_note: myDSS is Missouri's online portal for applying for MO HealthNet (Medicaid), SNAP, temporary cash assistance, and child care help.
missouri.agency_name: Missouri Department of Social Services (Family Support Division and MO HealthNet Division)
missouri.state_note: Most SNAP applicants must complete an interview, usually by phone, and the state aims to decide SNAP applications within 30 days or within 7 days for urgent cases.

montana.medicaid_note: Montana expanded Medicaid, so adults ages 19-64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify for Montana Medicaid.
montana.apply_note: apply.mt.gov is Montana's online benefits portal, where one application covers Medicaid, SNAP, cash assistance, and Healthy Montana Kids.
montana.agency_name: Montana Department of Public Health and Human Services (DPHHS)
montana.state_note: One application at apply.mt.gov covers Medicaid, SNAP, and cash aid together, and expedited SNAP can be approved within 7 days for households with very little money.

nebraska.medicaid_note: Nebraska expanded Medicaid, so adults ages 19-64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify.
nebraska.apply_note: iServe Nebraska is the state's online portal, where one application covers Medicaid, SNAP food assistance, energy help, child care, and other benefits.
nebraska.agency_name: Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS)
nebraska.state_note: iServe Nebraska is the newer single application that replaced the older ACCESSNebraska system, and expedited SNAP can be approved in as little as 7 days for households with little or no income.

nevada.medicaid_note: Nevada expanded Medicaid, so adults ages 19-64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify.
nevada.apply_note: Access Nevada is the state's online portal for applying for Medicaid, SNAP, TANF cash assistance, and other benefits.
nevada.agency_name: Nevada Department of Health and Human Services, Division of Welfare and Supportive Services (DWSS)
nevada.state_note: A SNAP application with just your name, address, and signature counts as filed that day, and households with little or no money may get SNAP within 7 business days.

new_hampshire.medicaid_note: New Hampshire expanded Medicaid through the Granite Advantage Health Care Program, covering adults ages 19-64 with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level.
new_hampshire.apply_note: NH EASY is New Hampshire's online benefits portal, where one application covers Medicaid, SNAP, cash assistance, and child care.
new_hampshire.agency_name: New Hampshire Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS)
new_hampshire.state_note: Starting January 1, 2027, most Granite Advantage adults will have to meet work or community-engagement rules to keep their Medicaid coverage, so check the DHHS Stay Covered page before applying.

new_jersey.medicaid_note: New Jersey expanded Medicaid, so adults with income up to 138% of the federal poverty level qualify for NJ FamilyCare, the state's combined Medicaid and children's health insurance program.
new_jersey.apply_note: MyNJHelps is New Jersey's online application portal for NJ FamilyCare (Medicaid), NJ SNAP, and cash assistance, and NJHelps.org offers a quick screening tool first.
new_jersey.agency_name: New Jersey Department of Human Services (Division of Medical Assistance and Health Services for NJ FamilyCare; Division of Family Development for SNAP)
new_jersey.state_note: New Jersey delivers benefits through county Boards of Social Services, so your county agency handles the application, and NJ SNAP guarantees a minimum monthly benefit of $95.
